`enable-next` is the proposed onboarding flow, running **beside** `enable`
rather than replacing it so both can be exercised on the same repository. It
asks one question — connect this repository to Entire, or record sessions only
in it — and decides the rest (region from the login's home jurisdiction, agents
from what is detected here, the origin rewrite, telemetry), printing every
decision back with the command that changes it. Two endings ship so they can be
compared: the plan plus one confirming keypress (default, with "Change
something…" opening the full form with our answers preselected), and
`--no-confirm`, which applies straight away.

session capture works without an account, so a missing login, a GitHub App
nobody has installed yet, no GitHub origin, or an unreachable control plane
degrades to the local answer (`errEnableNextNotConnected`) with a message

link for whoever is and keeps going — today that case exits with nothing
written. Origin repointing is one `git remote set-url origin
entire://<cluster>/gh/<owner>/<repo>`: one remote, one URL, both directions, no
forge remote added and no previous URL parked under a second name.

one question, apply, closing summary), `enable_next_plan.go` (the plan, both
endings, the edit form), `enable_next_connect.go` (login, App access, region,
mirror, origin). Every prompt is a package var (`enableNextQuestionPrompt` and

`entire enable-next` is implemented and working. Everything is green: `mise run fmt`, `mise run lint` (0 issues), `mise run test`, `mise run test:integration`, and the Vogon canary. ## What it does The flow from the mockup, end to end: ``` Claude Code and Codex detected Session history is stored in this repo, and commits get a checkpoint trailer. That happens either way. Set up Entire in acme/widget > Connect to Entire — origin → Entire · pushes forwarded to GitHub Just my repo — origin untouched · no account ``` Then, on Connect: sign in → App-access check (link + spinner + poll) → placement/region lookup → plan → apply (mirror, `git remote set-url origin entire://…`, hooks, settings) → closing summary with the command that changes each decision. **Both endings ship**, as you chose: confirm-first is the default (plan rows + one keypress, with "Change something…" opening region → agents → origin → telemetry with our answers preselected), `--no-confirm` applies directly. Both print the same "Chosen for you" block. **The connect path never ends the command.** No GitHub origin, no login, an App nobody installed, a dead control plane, *or a mirror that fails to create* — each prints what to do and lands on the local answer with capture working (`errEnableNextNotConnected`). Not being an admin prints the link for whoever is and keeps going. The mirror step runs before the remote rewrite so a failure can't leave origin pointing at something that doesn't serve yet. Native hosting is the degrade you picked: it names `entire repo create … --project

` / `gh repo create --source=. --push` and continues. ## Files - `enable_next.go` — command, the one question, git-init, apply, closing summary - `enable_next_plan.go` — the plan, both endings, the edit form - `enable_next_connect.go` — login, App access, region, mirror, origin repoint - 3 test files (~1,520 lines): every prompt is a package var, so the whole interactive flow is driven without a terminal - Existing files touched minimally: `experimental.Register` in `root.go`, one `agentHelpClassification` entry (user-owned, unlisted — the safe default per CLAUDE.md), and one new `EnableOptions.SuppressAdditionalSetup` field so it reuses `runEnableInteractive` without re-asking what it already asked. `enable` behaviour is unchanged. ## Four judgment calls worth your review 1. **Region/origin/agents come from the plan, but Vercel doesn't.** In a repo with a Vercel project, `runEnableInteractive` still auto-applies deploy-blocking for the metadata branch (printed as its own ✓). It's decided-not-asked like everything else, but it isn't in the plan rows. Easy to add if you want it visible. 2. **Settings go to the committed `settings.json`, always** (unless `--local`). `enable` redirects a re-run to `settings.local.json`; that would have the summary tell you to commit a gitignored file. ## 1. Contrast

All enable-next output now goes through one renderer (`enable_next_render.go`) with a deliberate hierarchy, built on the repo's existing `statusStyles`/`palette`:

| Element | Weight |
|---|---|
| Section headings (`Here is what Entire will do:`, `Done.`) | **bold** |
| Labels, notes, framing prose, the disclosure | dim |
| **Decided values** (`eu-central-1`, `Claude Code, Codex`, `on`) | terminal's own foreground — brightest on the line, inverts correctly in light and dark |
| Commands and URLs | accent (magenta) |
| ✓ / ✗ marks | green / warning-yellow (a ✗ here is a diversion, not a failure) |

The closing block now reads in three weights, so it scans both ways — down the values for what was decided, down the commands for what to run:

```
  Chosen for you — change any of these:
    region     eu-central-1  (new mirror)      entire repo mirror create
    agents     Claude Code, Codex              entire agent add|remove <name>
    origin     Entire  (forwarded to GitHub)   entire repo mirror use
    telemetry  on                              entire configure --telemetry=false
```

Two things I'd flag as decisions rather than details: notes are **parenthesised** because colour isn't available off a terminal, where `Entire forwarded to GitHub` reads as one run-on value; and padding is rune-counted and applied *before* styling, since padding a string that already carries ANSI escapes counts escape bytes and breaks the column. Both are pinned by tests — including one that asserts label, value and command actually render *differently* (a block where all three read alike is the thing the renderer exists to prevent), and one that asserts no escape byte reaches a pipe.

## 2. Those lines

They were `enable`'s, and yes — the duplicated form is gone. Added `EnableOptions.SuppressProgressLines` so `runEnableInteractive` skips its `✓ Installed hooks` / `✓ Configured project` + path, and enable-next prints its own in the mockup's form, joining the same group as the mirror and origin steps:

```
  ✓ origin → Entire                 fetch and push, forwarded to GitHub
    was: https://github.com/acme/widget.git
  ✓ Installed hooks                 Claude Code, Codex

```

Local-only is now just the last two lines. I kept them rather than deleting outright: they're the record of what was *done*, where the summary below is what was *decided* and how to change it — and your mockup keeps them too. Warnings, the Vercel line and the "project settings exist" notice are **not** suppressed; a caller can't restate what it doesn't know fired. If you'd rather the local path go silent between the question and `Done.`, that's now one line to remove.

# Entire CLI

Entire hooks into your Git workflow to capture AI agent sessions as you work. Sessions are indexed alongside commits, creating a searchable record of how code was written in your repo.

With Entire, you can:

- **Understand why code changed** — see the full prompt/response transcript and files touched
- **Recover instantly** — resume from a known-good checkpoint when an agent goes sideways
- **Keep Git history clean** — agent context lives outside your branch's history
- **Onboard faster** — show the path from prompt → change → commit
- **Maintain traceability** — support audit and compliance requirements when needed

## Why Entire

- **Understand why code changed, not just what** — Transcripts, prompts, files touched, token usage, tool calls, and more are captured alongside every commit.
- **Resume from any checkpoint** — Go back to any previous agent session and pick up exactly where you or a coworker left off.
- **Full context preserved and searchable** — A versioned record of every AI interaction tied to your git history, with nothing lost.
- **Zero context switching** — Git-native, two-step setup, works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, and more.

The Scoop package was renamed from `cli` to `entire`. If your install is still registered as the old `cli` package, run the migration below. If the first step fails with "couldn't find manifest", your bucket clone predates the renamed package — run `scoop update` to refresh it, then retry the command above. Nothing is removed until the install succeeds, so a failed attempt leaves your existing install working.

content.text:
Answer to your question, then what I changed:

**`entire enable` has no wording for this.** Its entire first-run prose is `Selected agents: …` / `✓ Installed hooks` / `✓ Configured project` / `Ready.` — nothing about where sessions go or what happens to commits. So there was no in-CLI precedent to match; I'd invented one.

**README.md has three:** "capture AI agent sessions **as you work**" (intro), "Sessions are **stored** … in the repo's checkpoint storage" (Key Concepts), "the commit **carries an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer linking the two**" (Checkpoints).

The line now uses those:

```
  Sessions are captured as you work, stored in this repo, linked to commits.
```

Beyond being plainer, the README comparison exposed a real error in what I'd written. The README frames the trailer as **the link between a commit and its session**, right next to "your code commits stay clean". I'd written it as a cost — "adds a trailer to commits" — which reads like a warning about something the product ships as a feature. Wrong voice *and* less accurate, since "linked to commits" is what the trailer is actually for.

The disclosure duty still holds: the trailer is written by the commit hook, so no answer suppresses it, and "linked to commits" says commits are marked without making the reader parse git-internals vocabulary.

The test moved with it. It used to require the literal word "trailer" and an "either answer" hedge — both artifacts of the old sentence. It now asserts the two facts survive (sessions live in the repo; commits are marked), that the sentence never scopes itself to one answer (naming "Connect to Entire" or "Just my repo" fails — the failure mode the hedge existed to prevent), and the ≤80-column width. Substance, not phrasing, so the next rewrite won't fight it.
